transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dave Mattingly.
This is Black Friday across the U.S.
The National Retail Federation estimates 126 million people will be shopping on this day
after Thanksgiving.
The retail group says it expects holiday sales to jump 4.2 percent during November and December
compared to the same period last year.
Much of that is because of higher prices.
NPR's Stephen Bassaha says the NRF also expects artificial intelligence to play a big role
in holiday shopping.
Traditional online shopping is all about finding the right keyword.
AI shopping is more about vibes.
The conversations you can have are, "Here's a style that I know my cousin is into and
I need to find a gift for them."
Emily Pfeiffer, a forester, advises retailers about AI commerce.
She says just remember when writing an AI prompt to be as specific and clear as possible.
It's best if you imagine that it's a young child who will probably misinterpret your
request.
Pfeiffer also warns you should not assume AI will find you the best price.
Like with human shoppers, AI needs time for deal hunting.
And be careful what private data you share with AI.
Stephen Bassaha, NPR News.
President Trump has signed a major disaster declaration for the state of Florida following
weeks of rainfall and widespread flooding.
It's been raining continuously.
It's the craziest thing.
It's stopped now.
It's very unusual for Florida, but it's record-setting rains in a lot of areas in Florida.
We're beating up pretty badly and we're releasing immediate funding.
The president was speaking yesterday at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Palm Beach.
The National Weather Service says some areas of central and south Florida have received
up to two feet of rain since late October.
A petition is circulating in Ottawa that calls for the ouster of the U.S. ambassador to Canada
amid accusations he's been abusive and insulting to the country.
As Dan Carpenschuck reports, the petition was originally introduced by a member of parliament
who belongs to the Green Party.
The move to oust U.S. Ambassador Pete Hoekstra comes as Canadians feel more pressure from
President Trump's tariffs.
The petition itself can't force anyone out of Canada, but it's a gauge of where relations
between Canada and the U.S. stand, and the continued friction over President Trump's
tariffs.
Hoekstra has made comments that rankled many Canadians, such as criticizing the elbows-up
rhetoric over standing up to Washington on trade issues.
He also publicly took exception to the dispute being called a trade war.
And he echoed Trump's remarks about the U.S. not needing Canada.
Nearly 290,000 Canadians signed the online petition asking Ottawa to oust Hoekstra.
Once the petition is tabled in the Canadian Parliament, the government has 45 days to
respond.
For NPR News, I'm Dan Carpenschuck in Toronto.
This will be a shortened day of trading on Wall Street.
Stock futures are sharply higher.
This is NPR News.
According Kenya says the government acted unconstitutionally when it built an Ebola quarantine center
with the help of the U.S.
As NPR's Jewel Bright reports, the facility has been the focus of protests and legal challenges.
The court said Kenya's government broke the law by failing to consult local residents
before signing an agreement with the U.S. to build a facility in their town.
The presiding judge ordered officials to stop work until the government discloses details
of the agreement.
The 50-bed facility was first proposed by U.S. officials in May as a quarantine center
for Americans returning to the U.S. after visiting Ebola-affected countries in Africa.
Kenya's President William Bruto has defended his decision to approve the facility, telling
reporters in June that the approval followed a request from President Trump.
Jewel Bright, NPR News, Vegas.
In Iraq, the government has begun closing border crossings run by Kurdish forces.
They include a crossing with Syria and another with Iran.
It's an effort by Baghdad to retake control of the crossings from the Kurdish regional
government.
The Kurds broke away from Iraq's central government in 1992 when Saddam Hussein was
president.
The closers followed this week's announcement from Iraq's prime minister that the Federal
Oil Ministry would now run some of the largest oil fields now operated by the Kurdistan regional
government.
AAA says the price of regular gasoline in the U.S. has now fallen more than 70 cents
a gallon over the last month.
It's averaging about $3.55.
I'm Dave Mattingly, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Black Friday shopping expected to draw 126 million people, with AI playing bigger role
President Trump signs major disaster declaration for Florida after weeks of record flooding rains
Petition calling for ouster of U.S. Ambassador Pete Hoekstra gains nearly 290,000 signatures in Canada
Kenya's court rules government acted unconstitutionally in building U.S.-backed Ebola quarantine center
Iraq's government begins closing Kurdish-run border crossings with Syria and Iran
AAA reports U.S. regular gasoline prices down more than 70 cents a gallon in a month
